response.title: My RV sits in a storage lot with no power, what solar setup keeps the battery from dying?
response.answer:
For an RV sitting in a storage lot with no shore power, I'd recommend a 100W solar panel with a solar charge controller to keep the battery charged while you're away.

You don't need a large solar system if your goal is simply to prevent the battery from dying during storage.

What solar setup do you need?
Shop

100W solar panel

My default recommendation for maintaining a typical 12V RV house battery. A 50W panel may suffice with the battery disconnected from RV loads, while 200W provides more margin for cloudy weather or small ongoing loads.

Shop

Solar charge controller

Essential for preventing overcharging. An MPPT controller is efficient and can automatically maintain the battery at the appropriate voltage. Choose one compatible with your battery chemistry.

Shop

Mounting and wiring

A permanently roof-mounted panel is usually best for storage. A portable panel works too if the lot permits it and it can be secured against theft and wind.

How it connects

100W solar panel

MPPT charge controller

RV 12V battery

Install a properly sized fuse near the battery positive terminal. Follow the controller's specified connection order.

Important: RVs often have parasitic electrical loads from electronics, detectors, and control boards. These can drain a battery even when you're not using the RV. Turning off those loads with a battery disconnect can make a small solar setup much more effective.

Two setups worth considering

Renogy 100-Watt 12-Volt Monocrystalline Solar RV Kit - with …

Complete rooftop solar kit with PWM controller

$199.00

The Home Depot

Victron MPPT 75/15 - SmartSolar Charge Controller - SCC07501…

Higher-efficiency controller with Bluetooth monitoring; requires a separate solar panel and wiring

$69.29

VoltaconSolar

One important distinction: the house battery and engine starting battery may be separate. A solar panel charging the house battery won't necessarily maintain the starting battery.

Also, if your battery is lithium (LiFePO4), the charging and storage strategy differs from lead-acid, especially in freezing temperatures.
